4.author: St. Augustine of Hippo
4.work: Tractates on the Gospel of John, Tractate 7
4.text: Augustine spent years preaching on the question Christ asks Saul on the Damascus road. 'Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou Me?' The Lord does not say 'why persecutest thou My people' or 'My Church.' He says Me. Augustine reads this as the foundation of the doctrine of the Body of Christ: the head and the members are so joined that what is done to one is done to the other. The Christian who suffers persecution suffers in Christ; Christ feels every stone thrown at the least of His own.

4.author: St. John Chrysostom
4.work: Homilies on the Acts of the Apostles, Homily 19
4.text: Chrysostom notices the doubling: 'Saul, Saul.' Christ does not do this often. He doubled the name once for Martha, once for Simon Peter, and now for the persecutor on the road to Damascus. The repetition, Chrysostom says, is the tenderness of God at the very moment of His severity. Saul is on a mission of violence; the Voice that stops him does not curse him, does not strike him dead, calls him by name twice as a mother wakes a sleeping child.
